title: Smoke over the Hills
author: draft 03/10/2026; rewritten 04/10/2026 as the worked example of a branching tale (expose, confront, keep silent)

binds.giver: a lord whose village was burned
binds.rival: the leader of another house of the giver's own realm

stages.journal: {giver} wants proof of who burned the farms of {village}.
stages.canvas: The lord is furious and certain: the realm's enemies did this. He wants proof to lay before the realm, so the war is pressed where it hurts.
facts: Farms around {village} were burned within the last weeks.
The lord is sure the realm's enemies did it.
He wants proof he can show the realm.

{giver}: Farms around your village {village} were burned. You are sure the realm's enemies did it, and you want proof to lay before the realm.

stages.journal: Ask the people of {village} who burned their farms.
stages.canvas: Shaken survivors, glad someone asks. Their answers do not quite fit the lord's certainty.
facts: The raiders came by night, few in number, well mounted.
They spoke the tongue of this realm, not the enemy's.
Someone hid a torn surcoat found in a burned barn.

locals_of:{village}: Raiders burned your farms by night; there were few of them, well mounted.
Strangely, they spoke like folk of this realm, not like the enemy.
Someone found a torn surcoat in a burned barn and hid it among the ashes, afraid of what it means.
Raiders who spoke like folk of this realm burned your farms by night.
A torn surcoat lies hidden among the ashes of a barn; the lord's champion is looking into it.

stages.journal: Look through what the fire left.

scene.title: The burned barns of {village}

opening.canvas: Grey morning over the blackened barns. A villager leads the player to where the surcoat was hidden, then waits at a distance. End by asking what they do.
facts: The barns burned down to their stone footings; the smell of wet ash hangs over everything.
Something is wrapped in sacking under a fallen beam.

findings.text: A household rider's surcoat, torn and scorched, in the colours of {rival}'s house.
Shod hoofprints in the mud behind the barns, heading north toward the realm's heartland, not toward the enemy's border.

hazards.trigger: climbing over the charred beams carelessly

scene.closing: Whatever the player did, they leave the ashes knowing the raiders wore the colours of {rival}'s house.

stages.journal: You know who burned {village}. What you do with it is yours.

{giver}: You sent the player to find who burned {village}, and you wait for their proof that the enemy did it.
{rival}: Your riders burned {village} to set the realm against its enemies, by your order. You speak of it to no one and turn the talk aside if it comes up; you never deny it outright.
locals_of:{village}: The lord's champion found something in the ashes. You do not know what.

choices.label: Lay the surcoat before {giver}
choices.canvas: The lord's certainty breaks. His anger turns inward, toward a man he sat beside at council. He thanks the player for the truth, though it is not the one he wanted.
facts: The raiders wore the colours of {rival}'s house.
It was made to look like the enemy's work.

{giver}: The player has just shown you a surcoat in {rival}'s colours from the burned barns of {village}: your own realm's house burned your farms and blamed the enemy.

{giver}.text: The player also saw hoofprints behind the barns heading toward the heartland, not the border.

choices.label: Take it to {rival} himself
choices.canvas: Shown the surcoat, the lord goes still. He neither denies it nor confesses; he wants to know what the player means to do with it.

{rival}: Your riders burned {village} by your order, to set the realm against its enemies. The player has just shown you one of your riders' surcoats from the ashes.
You neither deny it nor confess it. You want to know what the player means to do, and you would rather they kept silent.

choices.label: Keep it to yourself
choices.journal: Or keep it to yourself, and let the war go on against the wrong enemy.

{rival}: The player holds proof that your riders burned {village}. You would pay a good deal for their silence, and you wait to learn what they will do.
{giver}: You sent the player to find who burned {village}, and you still wait for their proof.

choices.label: Go to {giver} after all
choices.canvas: The lord's certainty breaks. His anger turns inward, toward a man he sat beside at council.
facts: The raiders wore the colours of {rival}'s house.

{giver}: The player has just shown you a surcoat in {rival}'s colours from the burned barns of {village}, and told you they went to {rival} with it first.

choices.label: Agree to keep silent for a price
choices.journal: Or name a price for your silence.

said.meaning: the player agrees to keep silent about the burning of the village in return for the rival's payment

choices.canvas: The lord pays, coldly. A debt of silence now lies between him and the player.

{rival}: The player has just agreed to keep silent about the burning of {village} in return for your silver. You pay it, and you will not forget that they hold this over you.

choices.label: Leave him to carry it
choices.journal: Or leave him to carry it.

exposed.memory: The player found that {rival}'s riders, not the enemy, burned {village}, and brought me the truth.

consequences.summary: Riders of {rival}'s house, not the enemy, burned the farms of {village}.

consequences.text: The player laid my riders' surcoat before {giver}.
The player came to me first, then went to {giver} all the same.
We learned who really burned our farms: riders of our own realm.
{rival}'s riders burned {village} and laid it at the enemy's door.

confronted.memory: I asked the player for proof over {village}, and they never brought it back to me.
confronted.journal: You left {rival} to carry what he did.

consequences.text: The player knows my riders burned {village}, and has said nothing to {giver}. Yet.

silence.memory: I asked the player for proof over {village}; none came.
silence.journal: You kept what you found to yourself.

consequences.text: The lord's champion asked questions about the burning, then nothing more came of it.

bought.memory: I asked the player for proof over {village}; none came.

consequences.text: The player took my silver to keep silent about {village}. They hold that over me now.

failure.memory: I asked the player for proof over {village}; none came.
failure.journal: The trail of the burning went cold.
